sections.title: Special Report

sections.text:
Item #1: The recent lunar eclipse on the Winter solstice was only the second such event in the last 2000 years, the other one occurring in 1638.
Item #2: The earth rotates about it's axis approximately 366.25 times for each revolution about the sun. 
Item #3: For points on the arctic circle, this (the winter solstice) is the one day of the year with 24 hours of darkness.
